newsitem.title: NORWAY: Exxon sees Balder oilfield start up delayed to Jun.
newsitem.headline: Exxon sees Balder oilfield start up delayed to Jun.

text.p: Start up of the Balder oilfield in the North Sea will be delayed by eight to 10 weeks while work is carried out on the floating production and storage vessel (FPU), operator Exxon Corp's Esso Norge said on Monday.
Esso spokesman Hugo Skandsen said the vessel would go into dry dock while modification work is carried out on the turrent area.
"We are evaluating various dry dock alternatives at the moment. That seems to be the best choice based on safety, quality, cost and schedule," Skandsen said.

"According to the plan for development and operation (PDO) we specified a start up window from the end of 1996 to the beginning of the second quarter 1997. We expect to be eight to 10 weeks behind the PDO, which means a delay from April to mid-June," he said.
The 4.7 billion crown Balder project will add at peak output 75,000 barrels per day to Norwegian production. Recoverable reserves are estimated at 170 million barrels.
The field is being developed using subsea wells tied into the FPU, it is the first dedicated installation of this type on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Crude will be offloaded from the production vessel and transported to market by shuttle tankers.
Esso is operator of the development and holds 100 percent equity in block 25/11.
